title: Noor and the Portrait
premise: When urban explorer Odile Montrose joins a survey crew mapping unmapped tunnels beneath the drowned quarter of Verrin Bay, they break through a door sealed from the inside—and find a portrait gallery of faces, each one a person the founders chose to keep alive. The frost spreading through the tunnels is a ledger: it preserves whoever the ritual names, and consumes everyone else, and the crew's presence has already written them into its pattern. As her teammates vanish one by one into the ice, Odile must decide whether to finish the founders' ritual—which requires naming a replacement soul for every life saved—or burn the gallery and accept that survival was never meant to be free. In the end she completes the ritual but writes her own name last, trading her place in the world for the found family she refuses to let the frost take.
about_author: Hazel Crane spent six years as a municipal archivist before turning to horror, a career that left her with an abiding distrust of buildings older than their paperwork. She writes from a coastal town whose tunnels she has never once been tempted to explore.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She maps the drowned quarter's storm tunnels for money, not mystery, and dismisses the crew's talk of passages missing from every city survey. When her instruments register a corridor where blueprints show solid rock, she assumes equipment error. Beat: competent skepticism established, first hairline crack of doubt.

chapters.title: Crew of Five
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. We meet the team: gruff foreman Dario, superstitious young tech Priya, brothers Tomas and Felix on the drill rig, and Odile holding them all at arm's length. Over cheap beer they joke about what they'll find. Beat: found family forming before the reader knows why it will matter.

chapters.title: Frost in July
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Deep in Tunnel 9, the air turns cold enough to see breath—in midsummer. Ice creeps along the walls in patterns too regular to be natural, like script. Dario orders a retreat; Odile insists on documenting. Beat: wonder curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew breaks through a brickwork plug and finds a door—oak, iron-banded, sealed from the inside with wax and wire. There is no handle. Priya refuses to touch it. Odile, telling herself it's just archaeology, cuts the wire. Beat: the point of no return crossed casually, almost carelessly.

chapters.title: Gallery of the Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Beyond the door: a long hall of portraits, dozens of faces painted in a style centuries out of date, each frame rimed with frost. Every subject looks warm, alive, mid-laugh. A ledger lists names beside dates of 'continuance.' Beat: awe and dread entwined—the rules of this world revealed as art.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He matches a portrait to a name from the town's founding records: a child who supposedly died in 1843, listed here as 'continued.' The math doesn't work unless someone paid for that continuance. Beat: intellectual horror—the crew realizes the ritual trades lives.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Felix's fingertips go grey and numb after he pockets a scrap of the ledger paper. The frost pattern on his skin matches a page of the book exactly. Doctors find nothing wrong. Beat: denial begins to fail; the supernatural makes itself personal.

chapters.title: Invisible No Longer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She researches the Montrose family name and finds her own great-grandmother's face in the gallery—a woman history says emigrated and vanished. Staying invisible, she understands, was always someone else's arrangement. Beat: personal stakes detonate; her skepticism becomes a wound.

chapters.title: Dario's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Terrified for his crew, Dario secretly visits the gallery alone and tries to strike terms with whatever listens there. The frost answers by writing his daughter's name into the ledger. Beat: power's corruption seeded—love twisted into leverage.

chapters.title: The Founders' Instructions
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Behind the final portrait they find the founders' codicil: the ritual can be finished or unmade, but either way it must be completed before the frost 'writes its final pattern'—a date the ice is visibly counting down to. Beat: clock started, structure of the endgame laid bare.

chapters.title: Tomas Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Tomas stops speaking, stops blinking; frost blooms across his eyes like cataracts. He still walks, still eats, but something in him is being read rather than living. Beat: grief and helplessness—the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Split the Crew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Dario wants to finish the ritual and save everyone; Odile wants to burn the gallery. The argument turns vicious, old loyalties weaponized. Felix sides with Dario because Tomas is already half-gone. Beat: the found family fractures under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Portrait Wants
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, dreamlike. Alone at night, Odile speaks to her great-grandmother's portrait and gets an answer—not words, but a memory pressed into her mind: the founders were refugees who bought their survival with strangers' names and never stopped paying. Beat: empathy for the monstrous; theme crystallized.

chapters.title: The Interim Pattern
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The frost spreads beyond the tunnels—ferns of ice on windows across Verrin Bay, always in ledger-script. The town notices. Officials arrive, ask questions, and leave with names of their own added to the book. Beat: stakes widen; power corrupts institutions too.

chapters.title: Felix's Choice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Desperate to restore Tomas, Felix attempts the ritual alone with a stolen page and his own blood. It half-works: Tomas wakes screaming, and a stranger in the hospital ward goes cold. Beat: good intentions as corruption; the price is now externalized onto innocents.

chapters.title: Ash and Argument
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile returns with kerosene to burn the gallery and finds Dario standing guard, wrench in hand. They fight—not physically, but with everything each has lost. She sees his daughter's name in the ledger and lowers the can. Beat: climax of the moral argument; neither side is clean.

chapters.title: The Final Pattern Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The countdown ends tonight: the frost reaches the gallery door, sealing it exactly as the founders sealed it—from the inside. Whoever is inside when it closes is kept forever. Beat: trap springs shut; no more time for philosophy.

chapters.title: Into the Keeping
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile, Dario, and Priya enter as the door seals behind them. The portraits are awake now, watching. The founders' voices—layered, patient—explain the terms one final time: finish the ritual, name replacements, walk out whole. Beat: claustrophobic dread; temptation offered plainly.

chapters.title: Names in the Ice
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Dario moves to write his daughter's name; Priya grabs his arm; the frost punishes hesitation by taking Dario's hand. Odile seizes the brush. Beat: climax of action—everything hinges on what she writes next.

chapters.title: The Last Continuance
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Instead of a stranger's name, Odile writes her own—trading herself so the ritual releases Tomas, spares Dario's daughter, and lets Priya and the others walk out. Her great-grandmother's portrait smiles, finally finished. Beat: sacrifice as answer to the price of survival.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew surfaces into ordinary morning. The frost recedes; the tunnels collapse behind them; Tomas weeps without knowing why. Dario holds his daughter and cannot say what it cost. Beat: bittersweet resolution—survivors carrying a debt they can't repay.

chapters.title: Noor
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Odile's POV from inside the keeping. She wakes in the gallery, warm, among the kept—no longer a portrait, but not gone either. On the newest canvas, a fresh face appears: a girl named Noor, laughing, alive somewhere above. Odile keeps watch. Beat: quiet, eerie grace—found family persists past death, and the cycle waits.
